Done. Saved both.

What this question exposed (generalizable):

The miss was 57.53 vs gold 57.50 — only 0.03 off, with correct data and correct method (H-spread = Q3 − Q1, Type 7 = numpy default). The failure was purely an instruction-parsing trap: the question said "use the intermediate values rounded to the tenths of billions BEFORE computing the H spread." That means round Q1 and Q3 to tenths FIRST, then subtract — not carry full precision and round only the final answer. Because two tenths-rounded values always differ by exactly X.X0, the correct answer's hundredths digit must be 0; my nonzero hundredths digit (.53) was the tell that I ignored the pre-round-intermediates clause.

Saved:
- Reference: appended a "QUARTILES / H-SPREAD with explicit intermediate-rounding" variant to descriptive-stats-over-months.md with the rule, the worked fail, the .X0 sanity check, Type-7 = np.percentile note, and unit-scaling/FY-window pitfalls.
- Memory: folded a compact version into the existing conflicting-rounding entry (memory was full, so I trimmed rather than added) so future runs surface the "pre-round intermediates → diff ends .X0" rule even without loading the reference.

This generalizes beyond H-spread to any officeqa question with a "round intermediate values to <precision> before computing" clause.
